headline: $783,003.88 network contract with ePlus approved for South Kingstown High School technology.
summary: The IT work covers network equipment, phones, and security cameras, and roughly $125,000 remains in a separate budget from construction. The project team said the building is on time and on budget, with substantial completion set for July 23rd, 2027. The meeting also swore in Alfred E. Bucco as police chief and approved a $19,500 engineering contract amendment for the Saugatucket Road culvert.
decisions: Approved the appointment of Alfred E. Bucco as South Kingstown police chief.
Approved the appointment of Charles Dickson to the Historic District Commission.
Approved the appointment of C. Stewart to the South Kingstown Veterans Memorial Park Commission.
Approved the appointment of Michaela Barden to the Conservation Commission.
Approved the appointment of William Rosen to the Conservation Commission.
Approved the appointment of David Brown to the Bicycle-Pedestrian Advisory Committee.
Approved a road race license for the Mews Tavern Gear 'N' Beer 5K on November 22nd, 2026, with a November 29th rain date.
Approved a Class F 19-hour beverage license for South County Health at the Mews Tavern Gear 'N' Beer 5K race.
Approved a temporary mass gathering permit for the Whiskey Wonderland at Sons of Liberty on December 11th and 12th, 2026, with a December 19th rain date.
Approved the final roster of 60 Revolutionary War-era Patriots and the inscription wording for the Brave Men as Ever Fought companion memorial.
Approved item 12C, an order of notice for a public hearing.
Approved a $19,500 contract amendment for the Saugatucket Road culvert engineering services, with a $5,000 contingency.
Approved $44,086.85 to replace cameras at the Peace Dale and Kingston libraries, plus a $5,000 contingency.
Approved high school technology contracts, including $783,003.88 for network infrastructure to ePlus.
Accepted the resignation of a registered agent for the Trustees of South Kingstown School Funds, effective December 31, 2026.
Referred Pond Street traffic and sign requests to the Town Manager's office.
discussion: Pond Street traffic: Residents asked for a three-way stop at Silver Lake Avenue, more speed and no-through-truck signs, and enforcement. Police said officers made 13 stops of commercial vehicles since the restriction passed, four for violations. Staff said a traffic study would test whether a three-way stop is warranted.

Polling places: Members discussed whether to reduce the 11 polling places and extend early voting hours. Staff said state law sets most election procedures, and members said fewer sites could hurt turnout.
Council president selection: Several residents urged the council to name the top vote-getter, Deborah Bergner, as president. One speaker said the council should choose its own leaders.

Veolia: Staff said Veolia has responded to recent questions, and a meeting with the town manager is expected next week, possibly on the 16th or 17th. Members discussed whether to hold an executive session first.

Extreme Airsoft lease: Speakers said the Peace Dale Mill is for sale and the business's lease will not be renewed. They must vacate by the end of January 2027 and are launching Operation Save Extreme to buy the mill.
